To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the index of microcirculation resistance before stenting was not related to the plaque morphology, whereas the index after stenting, but more importantly the change in the index after stent implant, was related to the degree of plaque disruption.

the index of microcirculation resistance after stenting in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarcted patients was related to atherothrombosis volume before stent implantation and to the reduction in atherothrombus volume during stent implantations, irrespective of the strategy used to measure atherothrombi volume by optical coherence tomographic imaging.

IMR measured before PCI was independent of the appearances on OCT of the culprit plaque within the infraction related artery, and IMR after stent implant was related to preprocedural ATV and the change in ATV during PCI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the culprit coronary artery morphology on the microvascular function after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in STEMI patients.
the influence of coronary plaque on final microvascular status after stenting in acute myocardial infarctions.
the relationship between IMR and the culprit coronary plaque morphology assessed using FD-OCT in STEMI patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the initial plaque morphology does not influence microvascular function before stenting, but it does influence microvascular function after successful stenting.

the initial plaque morphology does not have a significant effect on the IMR before stent implantation and the final IMR after stent implanting, but the change in IMRs after stenting is related with the degree of distalembolization.
FD-OCT is not useful in predicting the IMR in the acute setting of STEMI, however, FD-OCT can be used to assess the degree of distally embolized material during the stent implantation in STEMI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the culprit lesion characteristics do not influence IMR, but rather the amount of distal emboli that occur during stenting.
the initial plaque morphology of the culprit coronary lesion within the infarction-related artery is not a determinant of the microcirculatory function in patients with STEMI.

the final microvascular function in patients with STEMI is influenced by the degree of distally embolized material, which is related to the degree of atherothrombosis within the culprit plaque before stenting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the final microvascular function in STEMI patients after stenting depends on the degree of distol embolisation during stenting.
IMR after stent implant is related to the degree of distalembolization and the amount of plaque protruding into the lumen before stenting.
FD-OCT imaging of the culprit coronary artery before PCI is useful to predict the final IMR after stent implantations in STEMI patients.
